Senate."}},"codebook":{"definition":"Credit-claiming occurs when a senator presents themself as having caused, secured, delivered, authored, protected, funded, or otherwise materially contributed to a concrete governmental action, policy achievement, funding award, or benefit for constituents or another identifiable group.","clarification":"Code as credit-claiming when the release connects the senator's action to an achieved or officially approved result. Common signals include saying the senator 'secured,' 'delivered,' 'helped obtain,' 'authored' an enacted provision, 'worked to include' a provision that passed, or that an agency acted following the senator's request. Claims may be individual or shared with colleagues.
